topic: Anatomy of Persistent Memory: ContextNest vs Mem0 vs Zep

key_points: Frames the three tools as three complementary memory LAYERS, not rivals: Zep = session log memory, Mem0 = personalization memory, ContextNest = governed organizational context.

ContextNest (ctx): governed context — version-controlled markdown vaults, Git-versioned + SHA-256 hash chains, explicit steward approvals before LLM access. Ideal for dynamic org facts (pricing, inventory, customer relationships).

Mem0: personalization memory — semantic graph linking user profiles to preference nodes; autonomous semantic extraction from conversational streams at runtime. Ideal for persistent user preferences (IDE config, habits, favorite tools).
Zep: session log memory — message database with auto-summarization and message-indexing pipelines; continuous logging of raw user-agent conversation. Ideal for chat histories and dialog context.
Stale-fact traps: ContextNest = deterministic pruning via ctx forget; Mem0 = probabilistic graph overwrite can leave old+new facts active; Zep = logs summarize history, not validity.
Argues production agents should deploy all three together as a unified memory stack (Zep keeps continuity, Mem0 personalizes, ContextNest gates verified org truth).
HN traction: 23 points, published 2026-07-03.
Independent comparison of Letta, Mem0, Graphiti (Zep's engine), and Cognee across agent-memory design approaches.

Each picks a different answer to 'how should an agent remember across sessions': Letta edits plain text blocks/files; Mem0 keeps a vector store with entity hints; Graphiti indexes facts as time-stamped relationships; Cognee runs an entity extraction pipeline.
Positions Mem0 as a lighter vector-store + entity-hint approach vs Graphiti's full temporal knowledge graph.
Published 2026-05-28.
Mem0's token-efficient memory algorithm (April 2026): single-pass hierarchical extraction + multi-signal retrieval.
Benchmarks: LoCoMo 92.5 (up from 71.4), LongMemEval 94.4 (up from 67.8), BEAM(1M) 64.1, BEAM(10M) 48.6.
Mean tokens per retrieval call ~6,900 vs 25,000+ for full-context; latency p50 0.88-1.09s.
Biggest gains on temporal (+29.3) and multi-hop (+25.2) recall in LoCoMo.
Universal memory layer for AI agents; 63,940 GitHub stars (2026-08-24); actively developed.
Two products share one mental model: Mem0 Platform (managed) and Mem0 Open Source (self-hosted as library or Docker).
Y Combinator S24 company; integrates with 22+ frameworks (LangChain, CrewAI, LlamaIndex, Vercel AI SDK).
Plugins let Claude Code, Cursor, Codex harnesses remember projects.
Zep's engine for building temporal knowledge graphs ('Context Graphs'); 30,255 GitHub stars (2026-08-24).
Graphiti tracks how facts change over time, maintains provenance to source data, supports temporal awareness; unlike static knowledge graphs.
Zep positions as 'agent memory at enterprise scale' — governed Context Lake of temporal knowledge graphs, sub-200ms retrieval, three lines of code to add memory.
Continuously integrates user interactions vs traditional RAG; has an MCP server for Claude/Cursor.

stats.fact: Mem0 open-source repo has ~63,940 GitHub stars and is a Y Combinator S24 company.
Graphiti (Zep's knowledge-graph engine) has ~30,255 GitHub stars.
Zep serves prompt-ready context from a governed Context Lake with sub-200ms retrieval.

Mem0's new memory algorithm scores LoCoMo 92.5 (up from 71.4), LongMemEval 94.4 (up from 67.8), BEAM(1M) 64.1, BEAM(10M) 48.6, at ~6,900 mean tokens per retrieval (vs 25,000+ full-context) and p50 latency 0.88-1.09s.
ContextNest claims ~100x cheaper agent sessions by pre-digesting context into summaries (~500 tokens of relevant context instead of 50k tokens of raw files).
ContextNest organizes context as typed nodes with relationships, selector grammar, and versioned SHA-256 hash-chained audit trail.
Mem0 is a memory layer that persists across sessions, tools, and runs, for agents in Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, and 22+ frameworks.
Zep supports ingestion of chat, business data, and documents (threads, business data, batch ingestion) into its temporal knowledge graph.

angles: Three-layer framing: treat ContextNest/Mem0/Zep as complementary memory layers (session log / personalization / governed org context), not competing one-for-one products.

The stale-fact trap: probabilistic semantic memory (Mem0 overwrite, Zep log summarization) retrieves outdated + current facts together → hallucinations; deterministic governance (ContextNest hash chains + steward approval) prevents this.
Cost/efficiency angle: token-efficient memory (Mem0 ~6,900 tokens vs 25,000+ full-context; ContextNest ~500-token relevant context) as a cost optimization for agent sessions.
Governance & audit: ContextNest's SHA-256 hash-chained versioning and manual approvals vs Mem0/Zep's autonomous semantic extraction — enterprise/Compliance angle.
Architecture anatomy: what each tool stores (markdown vaults vs vector store with entity hints vs temporal knowledge graph), how facts are learned, and how stale facts are pruned.
Adoption reality check: Mem0/Graphtii have huge OSS communities; ContextNest is a young niche tool (15 stars) — position honestly as up-and-coming governance layer.
